articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.
• One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay must be wary of ‘untrustworthy’ ally Congress: BJP leader Ram Madhav
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “They blatantly lie. They want anarchy in the country. And most importantly, they are the most untrustworthy party,” the BJP leader said, referring to the Congress

BJP national vice-president Ram Madhav on Friday (November 13, 2026) extended a word of caution to TVK president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay regarding his ally, the Congress, saying it was the “most untrustworthy party” and that Mr. Vijay must “be careful.”

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Madhav said: “The leadership here [in Tamil Nadu] must remember that you are patronising a party, which is a party of anarchy, which is a party of liars. They blatantly lie. They want anarchy in the country. And most importantly, they are the most untrustworthy party.”

The people and politicians of Tamil Nadu were aware of the “untrustworthiness” of the Congress, Mr. Madhav said and added that DMK president M.K. Stalin “got to know about the Congress” six months ago and how “foolish” it was to depend on the party.

“Mr. Vijay also will get to know. He probably has some happiness now. All that is there. But, he must be careful... [if and when they see] greener pastures, they [the Congress] will immediately jump. Because they don’t have anything of their own. So, they will always survive on other parties.”

Mr. Madhav further said the people of Tamil Nadu have not forgotten what happened to veteran Congress leader and former Chief Minister K. Kamaraj of the Congress. The BJP leader said Kamaraj was instrumental in the bringing former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi to prominence, but she eventually “threw him out.”

Although the Congress and its leader Rahul Gandhi were trying to make it look as though the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was the target of the [ongoing] protests [in New Delhi and elsewhere in the country], Mr. Madhav contended that the “real target is Prime Minister Narendra Modi,” by propagating that elections were conducted in “wrongful manner.”

Replying to a query about the BJP’s advice to the TVK government about its alliance with the Congress, Mr. Madhav said: “The TVK is our adversary. We don’t give any advice. We will fight them politically.”

BJP State unit president Nainar Nagenthran reiterated there was “no difference between the [erstwhile] DMK government and the TVK government now”, pointing to the incidents of murder, dacoity, and rape in the State.

Referring to an issue allegedly involving TVK MLA and a District Collector , Mr. Nagenthran questioned: “If the Chief Minister is maintaining silence even for an issue like this, then for what will he speak out for?” Pointing to the Children’s Day celebrations organised by the TVK government, Mr. Nagenthran said: “Only his [Mr. Vijay] photograph is being publicised. How is it justified?”

articles.title: CM Vijay inaugurates distribution of cakes, greeting cards and sweet pongal to children
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Initiative marks Children’s Day, celebrated on November 14

Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Friday (November 13, 2026) inaugurated the distribution of cakes and greeting cards to children studying in government and government-aided schools, and sweet pongal to children attending anganwadi centres to mark Children’s Day, celebrated on November 14.

As many as 61,84,566 beneficiaries, comprising students, teachers and non-teaching staff of government and government-aided primary, middle, high and higher secondary schools, received the cakes at a total cost of ₹9.27 crore. Sweet pongal was distributed to 11,11,022 children aged between two and six, who are receiving pre-school education at anganwadi centres across the State.

An official press release said Mr. Vijay visited the Chennai Middle School in his Assembly constituency of Perambur and distributed cakes and greeting cards to 537 students (from LKG to Class VIII), and sweet pongal to 40 children attending anganwadi centres functioning within the premises. He also interacted with the students and the staff.

In Mayiladuthurai, Salem, Thanjavur, Madurai, Tiruvannamalai, Tiruchi, Coimbatore, Tiruppur, the Nilgiris, Erode, Namakkal, and Karur, students were provided two packets of cake each, weighing 45 grams. In the remaining districts, each student received a 45-gram packet of cake.

The distribution was carried out in coordination with the Chief Educational Officers, District Educational Officers, Block Educational Officers and Regional Managers of the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation. The quality of the cakes was assessed by the Food Safety Department before they were distributed to schools.

Mr. Vijay was accompanied by Minister for School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity A. Rajmohan, Minister for Social Welfare and Women Empowerment K. Jagadeeswari, Minister for Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Srinath, MLAs M.R. Pallavi and Revanth Charan, Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, IAS officers and other officials.

articles.title: Telangana approves 2,000 affordable houses for auto-rickshaw workers in & around Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Housing Board was cleared to adopt the same guidelines, beneficiary eligibility criteria, financial assistance, and other conditions applicable to Indiramma Indlu

Telangana government approved a proposal for taking up an affordable housing scheme exclusively for auto-rickshaw workers, in four areas in and around Hyderabad, on the lines of affordable flats at Indiramma Housing towers in Core Urban Region Economy (CURE).

Permission was given for construction of a total of 2,000 Economically Weaker Section (EWS) houses, with 500 each in Bandlaguda (LIG Colony) in Nagole; Gandamguda; Petbasheerbad and Jalpally or Laxmiguda. The societies would be titled ‘Auto Nagar Colony’, as per a government order (G.O.) issued on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The State Housing Board was cleared to adopt the same guidelines, beneficiary eligibility criteria, financial assistance, reservation provisions, selection and allotment procedures and other conditions applicable to Indiramma Indlu , with a specific condition that the beneficiaries shall be auto-rickshaw workers.

The Board would take up the scheme with an indicative project cost of ₹22 crore. It was directed to submit necessary detailed project reports and finance proposals after verification of land availability, site suitability and technical feasibility.

The State Revenue and Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said the project would be implemented through the Telangana Housing Board, with four housing complexes coming up at an estimated cost of ₹220 crore.

Mr. Reddy said the Housing Board had been directed to examine land availability, technical requirements and geographical suitability at the proposed locations and prepare detailed project reports (DPRs) along with financial proposals. The government would expedite the process to ensure that eligible auto-rickshaw workers could get houses at the earliest.

The Minister said the government was committed to providing housing security to every eligible poor family in the State. Under the Indiramma housing scheme, the government was extending financial assistance of ₹5 lakh to eligible poor families for construction of houses.

Describing a house as a source of dignity, financial security and confidence in the future for poor families, he said the Auto Nagar initiative was part of the government’s efforts to address the housing needs of specific occupational groups.
The government would continue its efforts until every eligible poor family in the State has a house, he said.

articles.title: India's Paytm gets preliminary RBI nod for wallet licence; shares hit record high
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Paytm Payments Services ‌will ⁠be able to ⁠offer prepaid payment instruments, including wallets, to customers after receiving the central ​bank’s final ‌authorisation, says company

India’s Paytm ​on Friday (November 13, 2026) received preliminary central ‌bank approval for its payments ​services unit to ⁠issue prepaid payment products, including digital wallets, sending its ‌shares to a record high of 1,960 ‌rupees.
Paytm Payments Services ‌will ⁠be able to ⁠offer prepaid payment instruments, including wallets, to customers after receiving the central ​bank’s final ‌authorisation, the company said in a filing.
The unit can offer these services ‌to customers after receiving ​the RBI’s final authorisation.

The approval comes ⁠more than two years after the RBI barred Paytm ‌Payments Bank from accepting fresh deposits and wallet top-ups over persistent regulatory non-compliance and supervisory concerns, effectively halting its ‌normal wallet operations.
Earlier, this year ​the RBI cancelled the banking licence issued to ⁠Paytm Payments Bank.
The latest ⁠approval allows Paytm’s wholly owned subsidiary to ‌move towards restarting wallet services.

articles.title: Special Summary Revision draft roll records 5.26 crore voters in Rajasthan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rajasthan has more than 5.26 crore voters as per the draft electoral roll published following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, according to figures released by the state election department.
The draft roll, published on Thursday (November 12, 2026), contains names of more than 5.26 crore voters -- with over 2.75 crore men, 2.51 crore women and 584 transgender voters.
The State election office on February 21 published the final roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), recording the names of more than 5.15 crore voters.

The two published figures show a numerical difference of 11.47 lakh. However, the SIR figure covered 199 Assembly constituencies, excluding Anta, while the latest draft has been released as a statewide total.
Rajasthan Chief Electoral Officer Naveen Mahajan said SSR 2027 is being conducted according to the Election Commission's schedule, keeping January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligibility.

According to the schedule, voters can submit claims and objections from November 12 to December 11. Electoral registration officers will dispose of the applications by December 28, and the final roll will be published on January 4, 2027.
Ms. Mahajan urged voters to check their names in the draft roll and submit applications if their names are missing or any corrections are required.

The department said copies of the draft roll have been provided free of cost to recognised political parties during meetings convened by electoral registration officers across assembly constituencies.
Political parties were given soft copies of the roll without photographs and hard copies for verification.
Voters can check their names on the election department's website or contact booth-level officers, who have been provided booth-wise copies of the draft roll.

During the claims and objections period, applications received will be compiled every week and displayed outside the offices of the electoral registration officers. The lists will also be uploaded on the department's website and shared with recognised political parties.
The department said Form 6 can be submitted for inclusion of names, Form 7 for objections to inclusion or deletion of names and Form 8 for corrections in electoral entries.

articles.title: Why RBI wants to cap select overseas remittances at ₹50 Lakh to save rupees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The RBI has reportedly proposed a ₹50 lakh sub-limit within the $250,000 annual Liberalised Remittance Scheme cap to curb dollar outflows and protect the rupee

The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%

India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Officials stated that DISCOMs would be evaluated for their performance over a five-year period, following by transmission, generation, renewable energy and RDSS.

The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.

The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.

Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.

Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.

Discoms have been selected for the first phase given their direct interface with consumers and the cascading impact of their financial and operational performance on other segments of the power sector and the wider economy.
The CAG will also rope in the coal department to facilitate an integrated assessment of the sector.

articles.title: Chinese company linked to Alice Huang obtained banned Nvidia chips: report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Alice Huang, mainly known as a former top executive at Megaspeed International, also founded Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, a company based in the eastern Chinese economic hub

A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang , the alleged spy for Beijing at the centre of the scandal surrounding Nvidia , obtained banned AI chips, Bloomberg News reported on Friday (November 13, 2026).
Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting to having extramarital affairs, including one reportedly with Alice Huang. China denies that she is a spy.
The scandal has raised concerns that high-end Nvidia microchips might have found their way to China, the United States' main AI rival, in circumvention of Washington's export restrictions.
Alice Huang is mainly known as a former top executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data center company that has drawn scrutiny over allegedly steering Nvidia chips to China.
However, she also founded Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, a company based in the eastern Chinese economic hub.

Bloomberg reported, citing an unnamed source, that Aperia Cloud Services, an official Nvidia partner headquartered in Singapore, purchased servers containing Nvidia's H800 chips from Dell Technologies.
Those servers later ended up in the hands of Shanghai Longteng, the financial news outlet said, citing documents submitted to the Chinese government.
It was not clear how the hardware was obtained or whether Alice Huang was involved in the deal, according to Bloomberg .
The United States banned the export of H800 chips to China in 2023, part of an effort to slow the development of AI technology by Beijing.

Megaspeed said on Thursday it was investigating whether it had complied with export controls on sensitive microchips. Malaysia has said it is probing a Megaspeed subsidiary over the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to other countries.

articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Chinese executive Alice Huang.

Jensen Huang resigned as Chief Executive Officer of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), bringing an end to his 33-year stint at the helm of the artificial intelligence giant he co-founded, following revelations of his extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.

Nvidia and Mr. Huang, are also facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News . He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.
The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who was allegedly recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia chief executive, according to The New York Times , which first reported that Mr. Huang was the target of an alleged espionage operation.
Few public details are available about Ms. Huang, also known as Huang Le. She reportedly held a senior position at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Microsoft explained that a portion of its infrastructure was 'experiencing elevated load' which it said was 'likely contributing to the connectivity errors'

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

An issue affecting Microsoft products worldwide was having a “serious impact” on Britain’s National Health Service (NHS), Rachel Harrison, public services head at the GMB union, said on Friday (November 13, 2026).

Staff receiving emergency calls were “unable to refer patient details in the normal way,” creating “a massive backlog,” though emergency and life-threatening call-outs “appear to be unaffected,” she said.
Microsoft ruled out “malicious” activity. The National Pharmacy Association said the outage was delaying prescriptions by affecting pharmacies’ communication with doctors’ offices.

Microsoft said that traffic was being gradually restored, with improvements in key customer scenarios, and that recovery actions had been completed across portions of the affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region. It said the focus was now on extending recovery across affected infrastructure in other regions.

“The Court is aware of the global outage affecting Microsoft systems. The Court is currently not receiving emails, but the Portal and contact forms are still functioning as normal. Parties and members of the public may not receive email notifications,” the Supreme Court of the U.K. tweeted.
Citing Germany’s approach, FOSS United CEO Poruri said the country had allowed individual regions to choose their email service providers, many of which use established free and open-source software.

India should adopt a similar approach instead of relying on a single provider, he said. Referring to the migration of government email services from the National Informatics Centre (NIC) to Zoho, he cautioned against replacing dependence on one provider with dependence on another.
Such diversification could also support domestic micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and strengthen the government’s Make in India initiative, he added.
The latest Microsoft outage should serve as a wake-up call for India to reduce its dependence on external technology service providers, Sai Rahul Poruri, CEO of FOSS United, told The Hindu.
Disruptions to email services, a cornerstone of professional communication, could result in significant financial losses for businesses, he said.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir: ‘More the bhakts comment, better it would do,’ says Rahul Gandhi on BJP’s criticisms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Responding to a question during an ‘Ask Me’ session on Instagram, Rahul Gandhi said, “It is a great book, they are all reading it. They can’t resist reading it and then they have got to comment on it”

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday took a swipe at the BJP leaders over their criticism of former AICC chief Sonia Gandhi's memoir, saying the more the "Bhakts" comment on the book, the better it would do.
He also claimed that a lot of the BJP leaders secretly like his mother and think she is fantastic "but unfortunately can't say it".

Responding to a question during an 'Ask Me' session on Instagram as to why the BJP is talking so much about Sonia Gandhi's just-released book "Belonging: A Journey Of Love", Gandhi said, "It is a great book, they are all reading it. They can't resist reading it and then they have got to comment on it."

"A lot of them actually secretly like her and they think she is fantastic, but unfortunately they can't say it. The other thing is - all you Bhakts, please please keep commenting on the book because the more you comment, the better it does. Ok guys," the Leader Of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said.
"Push it hard, be aggressive, be nasty, because that is what is helping her, Ok. Thanks guys," he said.
The book was released on Tuesday to a lot of enthusiasm from readers as they lined up at prominent bookstores in central Delhi to pick up copies of the memoir.

The BJP on Tuesday accused Congress leader Sonia Gandhi of trying to "justify" the imposition of the Emergency in 1975 and giving a "clean chit" to her husband Rajiv Gandhi on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in her memoir, and said her book "Belonging" should instead have been named "whitewashing".
Congress leaders have hailed the book for being candid and lauded Sonia Gandhi for her achievements.

articles.title: UN nuclear watchdog urges Iran to take 'steps' towards inspections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The International Atomic Energy Agency has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel and the U.S. launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites

The UN's nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take "incremental steps" to allow inspectors to return to key nuclear facilities in the Islamic republic, adding such access was "critical" in a report seen by AFP on Friday (Novemeber 13, 2026).

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel, joined by the United States, launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites.
Nuclear facilities have also been hit in the latest war, which erupted on February 28, and the IAEA has repeatedly called for access.
In its report, the agency said that it was "critical" for it to conduct "verification activities in Iran without further delay".
"The director general encourages Iran to consider technical and gradual measures by which conditions are achieved that allow for the return of agency inspectors to Iran," the report said.
The IAEA "acknowledged that the military attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities and sites created an unprecedented situation".

But because of a lack of cooperation "the agency is not able to conclude that there has been no diversion of declared nuclear material from peaceful nuclear activities in Iran", the report said, raising "serious proliferation concern" that "needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency".

The IAEA board in September referred Iran to the UN Security Council, marking the first time Iran has been referred to the UN top body in 20 years for failing to comply with its nuclear reporting obligations.

Before the June 2025 strikes, the IAEA calculated that Iran possessed approximately 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%, nearing the 90% needed to make a bomb and well above the 3.67% limit set by a now-defunct 2015 agreement with Iran.
Since June 2025, the fate Iran's nuclear stockpile has remained uncertain.
Iran has long denied striving to develop a nuclear bomb.
IAEA head Rafael Grossi said in June that the "widespread impression" was that the stockpile remains where it was before June 2025 near to the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP).

articles.title: Tanker carrying LNG hit mine, suffered explosion in Hormuz: Iran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Tankers are still facing attacks across the strait, ⁠despite a rebound in traffic and expectations of a de-escalation ‌in the US-Israeli war on Iran, that have been reflected in falling oil prices

Iran’s Revolutionary ​Guards navy said a tanker carrying ‌liquefied natural gas struck a ​naval mine and suffered ⁠an explosion in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday (November 13, 2026) while using what ‌they described was an “unauthorised and dangerous route”, state ‌media reported.

Iranian ⁠media reported on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that four oil tankers were hit by explosions in ​the waterway ‌vital for global shipping, adding that the vessels had ignored warnings and entered what it considers ‌restricted areas of the ​strategic waterway.
Tankers are still facing attacks across the strait, ⁠despite a rebound in traffic and expectations of a de-escalation ‌in the US-Israeli war on Iran, that have been reflected in falling oil prices.

At least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days ‌of November, after 37 attacks in October, ​which was the highest monthly tally since the conflict ⁠began in late February, according ⁠to data from the Washington Institute for Near East ‌Policy.

The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage drags on as company observes ‘limited recovery’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa

Microsoft Outlook suffered a major outage across the world Thursday (November 12, 2026), with tens of thousands of users struggling to access their email as the company said it was working "aggressively" to reduce the impact.

The disruption, which Microsoft attributed to "elevated load" on its infrastructure, dragged on for much of the U.S. workday and also affected other company products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
The disruption went global within a span of an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.
A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.
Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports "in the Americas," but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected "Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."
Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.
"We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company wrote on X.
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.
"We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."
In the United States, around 130,000 users reported issues with Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time (1800 GMT), according to Downdetector.
Outage reports have since declined, with about 37,000 users reporting experiencing issues with Outlook as of 6 pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT).
Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), ending his 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China .

The company’s board said Mr. Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

Editorial Context: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 13 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Without peace, Israel risks descending into chaos

Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.

articles.title: Restrictions on me arbitrary, vague: Sonam Wangchuk
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Ladakh administration shifted the activist from a protest venue to his residence in Leh and has been allegedly restrained from leaving his residence

Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk on Thursday (November 12, 2026) described the restrictions imposed by the administration on him as “bad in law, arbitrary, vague and disproportionate” and conspicuously “not using words such as house arrest”.

Invoking Section 163(1) of the BNSS, the Ladakh administration on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) evening shifted Mr. Wangchuk from a protest venue to his residence in Leh and has been allegedly restrained from leaving his residence.

“I was driven towards my village, where my residence is and was eventually taken to HIAL, reaching there at approximately 8.40 p.m. [on Wednesday]. I was told to remain at home under the supervision of police guards. Since that evening, dozens of armed police personnel [approximately 20 to 22] have been stationed at and around my residence,” said Mr. Wangchuk in a letter to senior officials of Ladakh and the Union Home Ministry.

Referring to the order issued by the Additional District Magistrate, Leh, Mr. Wangchuk said it disclosed no reasons justifying the necessity or proportionality of such an extended restriction, nor does it identify any continuing emergency or threat attributable to me that would warrant restraints of such duration.”

“The actions have clearly been taken to curtail my movement and rights before the election. The order is clearly bad in law, arbitrary, vague and disproportionate. I request you to kindly offer the clarification at the earliest, and withdraw this order without delay,” said Mr. Wangchuk, in the letter.
He claimed there was “no explicit order of house arrest or directing deployment of police personnel was shown to me then, and none has been served on me since”.

“I have not sought any security cover, and I am not aware of any threat to my person. No written order authorising this deployment has been furnished to me, and I do not know who directed it, on what date, or under what provision of law. I would be grateful to be informed of these particulars,” he added.

The Ladakh activist, who was arrested in September last year under the National Security Act (NSA) and released in March this year, said the Ladakh administration’s order “conspicuously does not use words such as “house arrest”.

“It does not use the words “detention” or “confinement”. It nowhere directs me to remain at my residence — a direction given orally to me by the personnel who picked me up and are now present outside my house. The order does not mention the scope or extent of the restrictions imposed on my movement, leaving their implementation to the discretion of the police personnel deployed,” said Mr. Wangchuk.

The alleged restrictions on Mr. Wanghuk came when Ladakh was preparing to hold polls for panchayat and municipality on November 21 and for hill councils on December 4. However, Ladakh’s key civil society bodies, Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), have organised protests and demanded postponement of council elections to April-May next year.

The authorities, in the order, directed that Mr. Wangchuk should be “refrained from engaging in any activity, organising or participating in any unauthorised rally, procession or public gathering or conduct that is likely to cause a breach of public peace disturbance of public tranquillity or obstruction to the peaceful conduct of the ongoing electoral processes within the territorial jurisdiction of Leh”.

articles.title: Palaniswami rejects speculation of Dhinakaran, Sasikala being readmitted into AIADMK
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Thursday termed as “unnecessary” a question about the possibility of readmitting AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran and former interim general secretary of the AIADMK V.K. Sasikala into the AIADMK.

“Please understand that they [Mr. Dhinakaran and Ms. Sasikala] have started their own parties. Please ask better questions,” Mr. Palaniswami said during an interaction with journalists at the Chennai airport.

To another query, Mr. Palaniswami said that the AIADMK was prepared to face any bypoll in the State and that the party candidate would win. Replying to another query, Mr. Palaniswami reiterated his charge that the TVK-led government was inefficient and that the law and order situation was deteriorating.

National & Polity Report: Palaniswami rejects speculation of Dhinakaran, Sasikala being readmitted into AIADMK. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and administrative governance framework.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary procedures, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and constitutional bodies responsible for upholding statutory mandates.

articles.title: No government school will be closed due to low enrolment: Minister Rajmohan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Thursday said that the State government will not shut down even a single government school on the basis of low enrollment of students.

In his inaugural address at the felicitation ceremony, organised by VIT Vellore, for headmasters of government and government-aided schools in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts that secured 100 per cent pass results in Board examinations for 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26, Mr. Rajmohan said that since the new government formed six months ago, no government school has been closed, citing low enrollment. “New teaching methods such as teaching mathematics through stories and improvements in curriculum have been introduced to boost enrolment in government schools,” he said.

G. Viswanathan, founder and chancellor, VIT, highlighted the need to set up a committee to study the impact of the Right to Education Act’s policy of ensuring pass results on overall educational quality and to examine whether the policy need to be reviewed. It comes in the backdrop of closure of around 94,000 government schools as against 51,000 private schools that were opened in the country in the past decade. “In Tamil Nadu, 246 government schools had been shut during the same period. At present, around 1,200 schools have zero enrolment,” he said.
Sankar Viswanathan and Sekar Viswanathan, vice presidents, VIT, and Premalatha, District Educational Officer (Vellore), were among others present on the occasion.

articles.title: Gang held for possession of 500 kg red sanders near Sholinghur in Ranipet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A gang of three persons was arrested after the Forest Department officials seized seven red sander logs weighing around 500 kg from a car near Sholinghur town in Ranipet district on Thursday.
The accused were identified them as S. Ramakrishnan, 39, V. Devinthran, 41, and T. Bhagyaraj, 35, all residents of Ranipet.

Officials said that they spotted a speeding car during a patrol led by forest range officer N. Saravanan in the Neelakandaranpet Reserve Forest (RF). The team tried to stop the car along with the help of police personnel, but in vain.

Forest officials and the police chased the car for around 500 metres and cornered the car at an isolated location near Sholinghur town. The team arrested the three persons after they found red sanders in the vehicle. Officials said that the accused told them the consignment was meant to deliver to agents in Chennai. The gang learnt the forests around Sholinghur town have a sizable number of red sanders that are cultivated by the Forest Department as part of an afforestation programme over a decade ago.

A case was registered and the gang members were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. The seized wooden logs were sent to the government incense sticks making unit in Tirupattur. Further probe is under way.
