articles.title: Theatre personality Prasanna resigns from special cell to promote rural industries in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a letter to Karnataka’s Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Prasanna highlighted closure of the Handloom Development Corporation and demolition of the Gandhi Ashram of the Badanavalu Khadi Kendra

Noted theatre personality Prasanna , who is also the founder of Charaka Multipurpose Industrial Co-operative Society, has resigned as head of the Mahatma Gandhi Vastrodyama Kosha, a special cell under the Department of Textiles and Handloom of Karnataka, which was set up to promote Gandhi-inspired rural industries. He cited recent developments concerning rural institutions.

In a letter to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar dated November 12, Mr. Prasanna said he was hurt by what he described as a series of setbacks to the rural development sector at a time when villagers were migrating to cities.

At Heggodu in Sagar taluk, he said, officials demolished a pedestal built to mark the dedication of a tank rejuvenated by Charaka, and the organisation was ‘unnecessarily accused of encroaching on the tank’. The tank had been dedicated by local MLA Belur Gopalakrishna after Ganga Pooja.

At Badanavalu in Mysuru district, he said, officials demolished the Gandhi Ashram of the Badanavalu Khadi Kendra about two months ago, against a Gram Sabha decision. He also said the government of Karnataka had closed the Handloom Development Corporation.

He told The Hindu that the Constitution envisaged village administration being carried out at the village level. Gram Sabhas were intended to function on par with legislative assemblies, and this principle had been recognised in the Constitution itself. However, it was not being implemented in letter and spirit, he said.

He was also upset that gram panchayat employees and officers were being treated as servants by tahsildars, deputy commissioners and ministers. Their opinions were neither sought nor respected, and the views of people living in the respective areas were not given due consideration.

Mr. Prasanna said the cell was conceived after then chief minister Siddaramaiah announced it in his Budget (2023-24) with a grant of ₹1 crore. It was to be a Section 8 company (under the Companies Act), with 51% of the shares held by participating institutions and 49% by the State Government. He said there had been no progress since then.
He said he would go on a hunger strike if the Chief Minister did not respond positively to the concerns raised in his resignation letter.

articles.title: Attack on CRPF post: Several suspects picked up for questioning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Immediately after the attack, security forces launched a massive cordon and search operation in the area to track down the terrorists
Several suspects have been picked up for questioning in the aftermath of the Kulgam attack in which three CRPF personnel were injured, officials said on Friday (November 13, 2026).
Terrorists opened fire at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) post in the South Kashmir district on Wednesday (November 11).
Immediately after the attack, security forces launched a massive cordon and search operation in the area to track down the terrorists.
The search operation continued on the third day, on Friday (November 13). The forces have erected barricades and deployed armoured vehicles at several places in the district.
Checking and frisking of vehicles is being undertaken at the security check-points as a tight vigil is being maintained, they added.
The security agencies are using human and technical intelligence to aid the operation, the officials said.
They said several suspects have been picked up for questioning by the police.
Senior officers of the police and other security agencies have visited the spot of the attack and reviewed security measures, the officials said.
Security has also been beefed up elsewhere in the valley as police and paramilitary forces conducted random searches of vehicles in Srinagar city and other districts of Kashmir.

articles.title: Civil society group urges Government to delink welfare benefits from electoral roll status
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citizens for Fraternity Forum urged the Government to issue a clear public assurance that electoral-roll status will not become a condition for receiving welfare benefits and that adequate safeguards will be established to prevent the exclusion of eligible beneficiaries

A civil society group has written to Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh over his reported remarks that voter ID will replace Aadhaar for identifying beneficiaries of social welfare programmes, urging the Government to assure the public that electoral-roll status will not become a condition for receiving welfare benefits.

Citizens for Fraternity Forum (CFF-Bharat) said it welcomed measures to improve transparency and accountability and prevent the misuse of public welfare schemes, but sought clarification on the use of EPIC/Voter ID and biometric authentication in beneficiary-related processes.

"We strongly believe that no eligible citizen should be denied welfare benefits merely because they do not possess a voter ID, their name is not included in the electoral rolls, or biometric authentication fails," the letter said.

articles.title: CPI(M) to boost its legal cell in Keralam to counter ‘fake news, misinformation’ targeting party
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Though CPI(M) already has a legal cell, it feels the need to further strengthen its activities considering 'the volume of misinformation being spread against the party' in recent times, says a party leader

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has decided to step up the activities of its legal cell in Keralam to counter what it perceives as fake news and targeted spreading of misinformation in social media platforms and public forums to discredit the party and its leaders.

A senior CPI(M) leader, who spoke on condition of anonymity, told The Hindu that though the party already has a legal cell, it felt the need to further strengthen its activities considering “the volume of misinformation being spread against the party” in recent times.

“Till now, we used to ignore many of these attempts to spread fake news and misinformation targeting the party. However, now we have decided that legal action has to be taken in all instances where it warrants one because there is such a constant flow of misinformation against the party on a daily basis these days,” said the leader.
The legal cell will have the active participation of senior High Court advocates as well as left lawyers’ collectives formed in all districts.

The extended Kerala State Committee meeting of the CPI(M) in September this year had discussed the issue and suggested corrective measures. Speaking at the meeting, CPI(M) General Secretary M.A. Baby had said that the “deliberate creation of a false perception against Left democratic forces” among the masses had played a key role in the reverses suffered by the party in Keralam in recent times. He also admitted that the Left should have been more alert in responding to the construction of this false perception.

Earlier this year, CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan had also come out strongly against a section of “corporate-controlled right-wing media”, accusing them of spreading false narratives and fake news to undermine the party as well as to scuttle the corrective measures being initiated within it following the Assembly election defeat.

articles.title: Microsoft Outage LIVE: Microsoft outage enters second day; company says not aware of malicious activity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Microsoft explained that a portion of its infrastructure was 'experiencing elevated load' which it said was 'likely contributing to the connectivity errors'

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

“When essential tools become unavailable, employees naturally look for ways to keep working,” Ben Mudie, field CTO of APAC Tenable, said. “The security risk is that temporary workarounds, such as personal email accounts or unapproved file-sharing services, can move sensitive business information beyond an organisation’s visibility and control. Disruption can also create opportunities for impersonation. An urgent request arriving through an unfamiliar channel, or a message offering to restore access, deserves extra scrutiny.”
He said that an outage alone does not establish that a cyberattack has occurred.

“But it does underline why business continuity and cybersecurity need to work together. Employees need clear, approved alternatives so they can remain productive without exposing company data or bypassing security checks,” he said.

“We’re seeing positive results for service stability and increased capacity as a result of our latest traffic optimization actions. We’re implementing these actions more broadly across affected regions as we seek to attain persistent recovery. A more comprehensive update can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin centre, as well as http://status.cloud.microsoft if the admin centre is not available to you,” the company said in a statement.

From Asia to the U.S., Microsoft’s outage involving services like Outlook and Teams has dragged on for hours and impacted many users, companies and some government operations as the technology giant struggled with fixing the issue.
More than 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook earlier on Thursday although new reports have since fallen from that peak.
Singapore’s Government Technology Agency said that government emails were down and that the agency is working with Microsoft to resolve the issue.
The Philippines’ Supreme Court said in a statement on X that the ongoing Microsoft 365 service outage has affected some of its operations, including email responses.
In Japan, Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki said the outage impacted the government’s IT infrastructure and that they were “keeping a close eye on the developments.”

Microsoft’s workplace services, including Outlook and Teams, remained disrupted for users in India and elsewhere on Friday (November 13, 2026), a day after a global outage began, with the company saying it was still working to pinpoint the cause and is not aware of any malicious activity behind it.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV denounces ‘machismo,’ demands women be protected in emotional return to Peru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Pope Leo called on the influential Catholic hierarchy to be models of unity and communion, and instructed Peruvian bishops to accompany their flocks and respond to victims of clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice

Pope Leo XIV on Thursday (November 12, 2026) denounced widespread “machismo” and violence against women in Peru, demanding that women be protected and respected as he set out marching orders for his beloved Peruvian church and people.
After his emotional homecoming Wednesday (November 11, 2026), the Peruvian Pope got down to business and turned to the challenges facing a church and country he knows well.

He called on the influential Catholic hierarchy to be models of unity and communion, and instructed Peruvian bishops to accompany their flocks and respond to victims of clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice. He also met with six survivors, including from an abusive sect-like group that Pope Francis suppressed last year.
Pope meets survivors of clergy abuse in Argentina as it reckons with legacy and ongoing cases
Pope Leo’s Argentina visit brings renewed scrutiny of clergy abuse scandals
But the 71-year-old Pope also showed himself to be positively overjoyed to be home and as relaxed as he has been in public since his 2025 election.

The Pope sang along enthusiastically as 40,000 people in Lima's Plaza Mayor serenaded him with “Contigo Peru,” a famous song from Peru's Pacific coast that celebrates national unity. He sang along later to another hymn, Alma Misionera (Missionary Soul), in Lima's stadium during a vigil along with 60,000 people inside and another 300,000 outside, according to Vatican estimates.
How can Pope Leo vote in U.S. elections while serving as the sovereign of Vatican City? | Explained

“It's a blessing not only for us Chiclayans but for all of Peru,” said Angel Esquives, a craftsman originally from Pope Leo's former diocese in Chiclayo who now lives in Lima. He said he left his home at 3 a.m. local time to go to the historic centre and stand in line to get as close as possible to the Pope.

Zozimo Perez came in a self-designed costume he named “the Inca Warrior,” with the pontiff's image on his chest and back. He was in tears as he saw Pope Leo stroll around the square. “This is a gift from heaven,” he said.

As he showed in the first two legs of his South American trip, the Pope was in fine form despite having undergone lung cancer surgery last month . He bounded up a steep flight of stairs Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning without any apparent problems and joked with the bishops that some “doubting Thomases” had predicted he wouldn't be able to come.
“But God is great and his grace is bigger than all of us and I'm very happy to be here with you,” he said to applause.

He called on the influential Catholic hierarchy to be models of unity and communion, and instructed Peruvian bishops to accompany their flocks and respond to victims of clergy sexual abuse with truth and justice. He also met with six survivors, including from an abusive sect-like group that Pope Francis suppressed last year.

Pope meets survivors of clergy abuse in Argentina as it reckons with legacy and ongoing cases

Pope Leo’s Argentina visit brings renewed scrutiny of clergy abuse scandals

But the 71-year-old Pope also showed himself to be positively overjoyed to be home and as relaxed as he has been in public since his 2025 election.

The Pope sang along enthusiastically as 40,000 people in Lima's Plaza Mayor serenaded him with “Contigo Peru,” a famous song from Peru's Pacific coast that celebrates national unity. He sang along later to another hymn, Alma Misionera (Missionary Soul), in Lima's stadium during a vigil along with 60,000 people inside and another 300,000 outside, according to Vatican estimates.

“It's a blessing not only for us Chiclayans but for all of Peru,” said Angel Esquives, a craftsman originally from Pope Leo's former diocese in Chiclayo who now lives in Lima. He said he left his home at 3 a.m. local time to go to the historic centre and stand in line to get as close as possible to the Pope.

Zozimo Perez came in a self-designed costume he named “the Inca Warrior,” with the pontiff's image on his chest and back. He was in tears as he saw Pope Leo stroll around the square. “This is a gift from heaven,” he said.

As he showed in the first two legs of his South American trip, the Pope was in fine form despite having undergone lung cancer surgery last month . He bounded up a steep flight of stairs Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning without any apparent problems and joked with the bishops that some “doubting Thomases” had predicted he wouldn't be able to come.

“But God is great and his grace is bigger than all of us and I'm very happy to be here with you,” he said to applause.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay must be wary of ‘untrustworthy’ ally Congress: BJP leader Ram Madhav
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “They blatantly lie. They want anarchy in the country. And most importantly, they are the most untrustworthy party,” the BJP leader said, referring to the Congress

BJP national vice-president Ram Madhav on Friday (November 13, 2026) extended a word of caution to TVK president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay regarding his ally, the Congress, saying it was the “most untrustworthy party” and that Mr. Vijay must “be careful.”

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Madhav said: “The leadership here [in Tamil Nadu] must remember that you are patronising a party, which is a party of anarchy, which is a party of liars. They blatantly lie. They want anarchy in the country. And most importantly, they are the most untrustworthy party.”

The people and politicians of Tamil Nadu were aware of the “untrustworthiness” of the Congress, Mr. Madhav said and added that DMK president M.K. Stalin “got to know about the Congress” six months ago and how “foolish” it was to depend on the party.

“Mr. Vijay also will get to know. He probably has some happiness now. All that is there. But, he must be careful... [if and when they see] greener pastures, they [the Congress] will immediately jump. Because they don’t have anything of their own. So, they will always survive on other parties.”

Mr. Madhav further said the people of Tamil Nadu have not forgotten what happened to veteran Congress leader and former Chief Minister K. Kamaraj of the Congress. The BJP leader said Kamaraj was instrumental in the bringing former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi to prominence, but she eventually “threw him out.”

Although the Congress and its leader Rahul Gandhi were trying to make it look as though the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was the target of the [ongoing] protests [in New Delhi and elsewhere in the country], Mr. Madhav contended that the “real target is Prime Minister Narendra Modi,” by propagating that elections were conducted in “wrongful manner.”

Replying to a query about the BJP’s advice to the TVK government about its alliance with the Congress, Mr. Madhav said: “The TVK is our adversary. We don’t give any advice. We will fight them politically.”

BJP State unit president Nainar Nagenthran reiterated there was “no difference between the [erstwhile] DMK government and the TVK government now”, pointing to the incidents of murder, dacoity, and rape in the State.

Referring to an issue allegedly involving TVK MLA and a District Collector , Mr. Nagenthran questioned: “If the Chief Minister is maintaining silence even for an issue like this, then for what will he speak out for?” Pointing to the Children’s Day celebrations organised by the TVK government, Mr. Nagenthran said: “Only his [Mr. Vijay] photograph is being publicised. How is it justified?”

articles.title: CM Vijay inaugurates distribution of cakes, greeting cards and sweet pongal to children
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Initiative marks Children’s Day, celebrated on November 14

Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Friday (November 13, 2026) inaugurated the distribution of cakes and greeting cards to children studying in government and government-aided schools, and sweet pongal to children attending anganwadi centres to mark Children’s Day, celebrated on November 14.

As many as 61,84,566 beneficiaries, comprising students, teachers and non-teaching staff of government and government-aided primary, middle, high and higher secondary schools, received the cakes at a total cost of ₹9.27 crore. Sweet pongal was distributed to 11,11,022 children aged between two and six, who are receiving pre-school education at anganwadi centres across the State.

An official press release said Mr. Vijay visited the Chennai Middle School in his Assembly constituency of Perambur and distributed cakes and greeting cards to 537 students (from LKG to Class VIII), and sweet pongal to 40 children attending anganwadi centres functioning within the premises. He also interacted with the students and the staff.

In Mayiladuthurai, Salem, Thanjavur, Madurai, Tiruvannamalai, Tiruchi, Coimbatore, Tiruppur, the Nilgiris, Erode, Namakkal, and Karur, students were provided two packets of cake each, weighing 45 grams. In the remaining districts, each student received a 45-gram packet of cake.

The distribution was carried out in coordination with the Chief Educational Officers, District Educational Officers, Block Educational Officers and Regional Managers of the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation. The quality of the cakes was assessed by the Food Safety Department before they were distributed to schools.

Mr. Vijay was accompanied by Minister for School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity A. Rajmohan, Minister for Social Welfare and Women Empowerment K. Jagadeeswari, Minister for Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare Srinath, MLAs M.R. Pallavi and Revanth Charan, Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, IAS officers and other officials.

articles.title: Telangana approves 2,000 affordable houses for auto-rickshaw workers in & around Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Housing Board was cleared to adopt the same guidelines, beneficiary eligibility criteria, financial assistance, and other conditions applicable to Indiramma Indlu

Telangana government approved a proposal for taking up an affordable housing scheme exclusively for auto-rickshaw workers, in four areas in and around Hyderabad, on the lines of affordable flats at Indiramma Housing towers in Core Urban Region Economy (CURE).

Permission was given for construction of a total of 2,000 Economically Weaker Section (EWS) houses, with 500 each in Bandlaguda (LIG Colony) in Nagole; Gandamguda; Petbasheerbad and Jalpally or Laxmiguda. The societies would be titled ‘Auto Nagar Colony’, as per a government order (G.O.) issued on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The State Housing Board was cleared to adopt the same guidelines, beneficiary eligibility criteria, financial assistance, reservation provisions, selection and allotment procedures and other conditions applicable to Indiramma Indlu , with a specific condition that the beneficiaries shall be auto-rickshaw workers.

The Board would take up the scheme with an indicative project cost of ₹22 crore. It was directed to submit necessary detailed project reports and finance proposals after verification of land availability, site suitability and technical feasibility.

The State Revenue and Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said the project would be implemented through the Telangana Housing Board, with four housing complexes coming up at an estimated cost of ₹220 crore.

Mr. Reddy said the Housing Board had been directed to examine land availability, technical requirements and geographical suitability at the proposed locations and prepare detailed project reports (DPRs) along with financial proposals. The government would expedite the process to ensure that eligible auto-rickshaw workers could get houses at the earliest.

The Minister said the government was committed to providing housing security to every eligible poor family in the State. Under the Indiramma housing scheme, the government was extending financial assistance of ₹5 lakh to eligible poor families for construction of houses.

Describing a house as a source of dignity, financial security and confidence in the future for poor families, he said the Auto Nagar initiative was part of the government’s efforts to address the housing needs of specific occupational groups.
The government would continue its efforts until every eligible poor family in the State has a house, he said.

articles.title: India's Paytm gets preliminary RBI nod for wallet licence; shares hit record high
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Paytm Payments Services ‌will ⁠be able to ⁠offer prepaid payment instruments, including wallets, to customers after receiving the central ​bank’s final ‌authorisation, says company

India’s Paytm ​on Friday (November 13, 2026) received preliminary central ‌bank approval for its payments ​services unit to ⁠issue prepaid payment products, including digital wallets, sending its ‌shares to a record high of 1,960 ‌rupees.
Paytm Payments Services ‌will ⁠be able to ⁠offer prepaid payment instruments, including wallets, to customers after receiving the central ​bank’s final ‌authorisation, the company said in a filing.
The unit can offer these services ‌to customers after receiving ​the RBI’s final authorisation.

The approval comes ⁠more than two years after the RBI barred Paytm ‌Payments Bank from accepting fresh deposits and wallet top-ups over persistent regulatory non-compliance and supervisory concerns, effectively halting its ‌normal wallet operations.
Earlier, this year ​the RBI cancelled the banking licence issued to ⁠Paytm Payments Bank.
The latest ⁠approval allows Paytm’s wholly owned subsidiary to ‌move towards restarting wallet services.

fullParagraphs: PM Modi to address students who have arrived to witness the inauguration of COSMOS LED Dome Planetarium

The opening of the elevated section of the Pink Line is expected to offer only minor relief to the city’s gridlock, with the crucial underground section connecting the Central Business District to north Bengaluru awaiting completion, writes Darshan Devaiah B.P. Mind the gap: Partial opening of Namma Metro Pink Line leaves commuters wanting Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.

India has seen many great astronomers, such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Nilakantha Somayaji. The advanced instruments and technology we have today did not exist back then. Despite this, they made major discoveries and carried out difficult calculations, said PM Modi after inaugurating the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru.

The facility features a 15-metre tilted dome comprising around 6,150 panels and 4.2 crore individual LEDs. It includes a Sky Theatre, exhibition halls, an astronomy museum and training facilities, with the aim of promoting astronomy education and public outreach.
As India achieves one scientific breakthrough after another, Mysuru is also adding a new chapter to India’s scientific journey with this state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium, he added.
Our government opened up the space sector. This has created new opportunities for the private sector. India’s startups have also been given an opportunity to showcase their potential.

Underscoring Karnataka’s contribution to India’s space programme, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the country’s space journey was incomplete without the State’s contributions, from Aryabhata, India’s first satellite, to Chandrayaan, Aditya-L1 and the ambitious Gaganyaan mission.
Recalling the contributions of the Mysore Maharajas to scientific development, the CM cited their vision that had resulted in the establishment of top institutions including the IISc.

Karnataka government is ready to support the Centre in establishment of new centres of excellence. We are ready to support and encourage young minds and develop skills to our engineering graduates, Mr. Shivakumar said.

Seeking PM’s support in bringing the Mekedatu project to life, Mr. Shivakumar also reiterated the State’s concerns over the Kasturirangan Committee report on the ecologically sensitive areas of the Western Ghats.

Raising concerns over primary education and migration to urban centres, the Chief Minister said economic migration for education and employment was leading to a significant shift in population patterns.

To address this challenge, he requested the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to issue advisories aligning corporate CSR initiatives with Karnataka’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CCSR) Guidelines. This, he said, would help upgrade 1,000 government schools into Karnataka Public Schools and strengthen the public education system.

articles.title: Special Summary Revision draft roll records 5.26 crore voters in Rajasthan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rajasthan has more than 5.26 crore voters as per the draft electoral roll published following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, according to figures released by the state election department.
The draft roll, published on Thursday (November 12, 2026), contains names of more than 5.26 crore voters -- with over 2.75 crore men, 2.51 crore women and 584 transgender voters.
The State election office on February 21 published the final roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), recording the names of more than 5.15 crore voters.

The two published figures show a numerical difference of 11.47 lakh. However, the SIR figure covered 199 Assembly constituencies, excluding Anta, while the latest draft has been released as a statewide total.
Rajasthan Chief Electoral Officer Naveen Mahajan said SSR 2027 is being conducted according to the Election Commission's schedule, keeping January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligibility.

According to the schedule, voters can submit claims and objections from November 12 to December 11. Electoral registration officers will dispose of the applications by December 28, and the final roll will be published on January 4, 2027.
Ms. Mahajan urged voters to check their names in the draft roll and submit applications if their names are missing or any corrections are required.

The department said copies of the draft roll have been provided free of cost to recognised political parties during meetings convened by electoral registration officers across assembly constituencies.
Political parties were given soft copies of the roll without photographs and hard copies for verification.
Voters can check their names on the election department's website or contact booth-level officers, who have been provided booth-wise copies of the draft roll.

During the claims and objections period, applications received will be compiled every week and displayed outside the offices of the electoral registration officers. The lists will also be uploaded on the department's website and shared with recognised political parties.
The department said Form 6 can be submitted for inclusion of names, Form 7 for objections to inclusion or deletion of names and Form 8 for corrections in electoral entries.

Rajasthan has more than 5.26 crore voters as per the draft electoral roll published following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, according to figures released by the state election department.

The draft roll, published on Thursday (November 12, 2026), contains names of more than 5.26 crore voters -- with over 2.75 crore men, 2.51 crore women and 584 transgender voters.

The State election office on February 21 published the final roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), recording the names of more than 5.15 crore voters.

The two published figures show a numerical difference of 11.47 lakh. However, the SIR figure covered 199 Assembly constituencies, excluding Anta, while the latest draft has been released as a statewide total.

Rajasthan Chief Electoral Officer Naveen Mahajan said SSR 2027 is being conducted according to the Election Commission's schedule, keeping January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligibility.

According to the schedule, voters can submit claims and objections from November 12 to December 11. Electoral registration officers will dispose of the applications by December 28, and the final roll will be published on January 4, 2027.

Ms. Mahajan urged voters to check their names in the draft roll and submit applications if their names are missing or any corrections are required.

The department said copies of the draft roll have been provided free of cost to recognised political parties during meetings convened by electoral registration officers across assembly constituencies.

Political parties were given soft copies of the roll without photographs and hard copies for verification.

Voters can check their names on the election department's website or contact booth-level officers, who have been provided booth-wise copies of the draft roll.

During the claims and objections period, applications received will be compiled every week and displayed outside the offices of the electoral registration officers. The lists will also be uploaded on the department's website and shared with recognised political parties.

The department said Form 6 can be submitted for inclusion of names, Form 7 for objections to inclusion or deletion of names and Form 8 for corrections in electoral entries.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Chinese company linked to Alice Huang obtained banned Nvidia chips: report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Alice Huang, mainly known as a former top executive at Megaspeed International, also founded Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, a company based in the eastern Chinese economic hub

A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang , the alleged spy for Beijing at the centre of the scandal surrounding Nvidia , obtained banned AI chips, Bloomberg News reported on Friday (November 13, 2026).
Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting to having extramarital affairs, including one reportedly with Alice Huang. China denies that she is a spy.
The scandal has raised concerns that high-end Nvidia microchips might have found their way to China, the United States' main AI rival, in circumvention of Washington's export restrictions.
Alice Huang is mainly known as a former top executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data center company that has drawn scrutiny over allegedly steering Nvidia chips to China.
However, she also founded Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, a company based in the eastern Chinese economic hub.

Bloomberg reported, citing an unnamed source, that Aperia Cloud Services, an official Nvidia partner headquartered in Singapore, purchased servers containing Nvidia's H800 chips from Dell Technologies.
Those servers later ended up in the hands of Shanghai Longteng, the financial news outlet said, citing documents submitted to the Chinese government.
It was not clear how the hardware was obtained or whether Alice Huang was involved in the deal, according to Bloomberg .
The United States banned the export of H800 chips to China in 2023, part of an effort to slow the development of AI technology by Beijing.

Megaspeed said on Thursday it was investigating whether it had complied with export controls on sensitive microchips. Malaysia has said it is probing a Megaspeed subsidiary over the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to other countries.

articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Chinese executive Alice Huang.

Jensen Huang resigned as Chief Executive Officer of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), bringing an end to his 33-year stint at the helm of the artificial intelligence giant he co-founded, following revelations of his extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.

Nvidia and Mr. Huang, are also facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News . articles.title: Microsoft Outage LIVE: Microsoft extends mail timeout to 48 hours as outage hits governments, organisations worldwide
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Microsoft explained that a portion of its infrastructure was 'experiencing elevated load' which it said was 'likely contributing to the connectivity errors'

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.

An issue affecting Microsoft products worldwide was having a “serious impact” on Britain’s National Health Service (NHS), Rachel Harrison, public services head at the GMB union, said on Friday (November 13, 2026).

Staff receiving emergency calls were “unable to refer patient details in the normal way,” creating “a massive backlog,” though emergency and life-threatening call-outs “appear to be unaffected,” she said.
Microsoft ruled out “malicious” activity. The National Pharmacy Association said the outage was delaying prescriptions by affecting pharmacies’ communication with doctors’ offices.

Microsoft said that traffic was being gradually restored, with improvements in key customer scenarios, and that recovery actions had been completed across portions of the affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region. It said the focus was now on extending recovery across affected infrastructure in other regions.

“The Court is aware of the global outage affecting Microsoft systems. The Court is currently not receiving emails, but the Portal and contact forms are still functioning as normal. Parties and members of the public may not receive email notifications,” the Supreme Court of the U.K. tweeted.
Citing Germany’s approach, FOSS United CEO Poruri said the country had allowed individual regions to choose their email service providers, many of which use established free and open-source software.

India should adopt a similar approach instead of relying on a single provider, he said. Referring to the migration of government email services from the National Informatics Centre (NIC) to Zoho, he cautioned against replacing dependence on one provider with dependence on another.
Such diversification could also support domestic micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and strengthen the government’s Make in India initiative, he added.
The latest Microsoft outage should serve as a wake-up call for India to reduce its dependence on external technology service providers, Sai Rahul Poruri, CEO of FOSS United, told The Hindu.
Disruptions to email services, a cornerstone of professional communication, could result in significant financial losses for businesses, he said.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir: ‘More the bhakts comment, better it would do,’ says Rahul Gandhi on BJP’s criticisms
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Responding to a question during an ‘Ask Me’ session on Instagram, Rahul Gandhi said, “It is a great book, they are all reading it. They can’t resist reading it and then they have got to comment on it”

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday took a swipe at the BJP leaders over their criticism of former AICC chief Sonia Gandhi's memoir, saying the more the "Bhakts" comment on the book, the better it would do.
He also claimed that a lot of the BJP leaders secretly like his mother and think she is fantastic "but unfortunately can't say it".

Responding to a question during an 'Ask Me' session on Instagram as to why the BJP is talking so much about Sonia Gandhi's just-released book "Belonging: A Journey Of Love", Gandhi said, "It is a great book, they are all reading it. They can't resist reading it and then they have got to comment on it."

"A lot of them actually secretly like her and they think she is fantastic, but unfortunately they can't say it. The other thing is - all you Bhakts, please please keep commenting on the book because the more you comment, the better it does. Ok guys," the Leader Of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said.
"Push it hard, be aggressive, be nasty, because that is what is helping her, Ok. Thanks guys," he said.
The book was released on Tuesday to a lot of enthusiasm from readers as they lined up at prominent bookstores in central Delhi to pick up copies of the memoir.

The BJP on Tuesday accused Congress leader Sonia Gandhi of trying to "justify" the imposition of the Emergency in 1975 and giving a "clean chit" to her husband Rajiv Gandhi on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in her memoir, and said her book "Belonging" should instead have been named "whitewashing".
Congress leaders have hailed the book for being candid and lauded Sonia Gandhi for her achievements.

articles.title: UN nuclear watchdog urges Iran to take 'steps' towards inspections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The International Atomic Energy Agency has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel and the U.S. launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites

The UN's nuclear watchdog urged Iran to take "incremental steps" to allow inspectors to return to key nuclear facilities in the Islamic republic, adding such access was "critical" in a report seen by AFP on Friday (Novemeber 13, 2026).

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel, joined by the United States, launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites.
Nuclear facilities have also been hit in the latest war, which erupted on February 28, and the IAEA has repeatedly called for access.
In its report, the agency said that it was "critical" for it to conduct "verification activities in Iran without further delay".
"The director general encourages Iran to consider technical and gradual measures by which conditions are achieved that allow for the return of agency inspectors to Iran," the report said.
The IAEA "acknowledged that the military attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities and sites created an unprecedented situation".

But because of a lack of cooperation "the agency is not able to conclude that there has been no diversion of declared nuclear material from peaceful nuclear activities in Iran", the report said, raising "serious proliferation concern" that "needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency".

The IAEA board in September referred Iran to the UN Security Council, marking the first time Iran has been referred to the UN top body in 20 years for failing to comply with its nuclear reporting obligations.

Before the June 2025 strikes, the IAEA calculated that Iran possessed approximately 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%, nearing the 90% needed to make a bomb and well above the 3.67% limit set by a now-defunct 2015 agreement with Iran.
Since June 2025, the fate Iran's nuclear stockpile has remained uncertain.
Iran has long denied striving to develop a nuclear bomb.
IAEA head Rafael Grossi said in June that the "widespread impression" was that the stockpile remains where it was before June 2025 near to the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP).

articles.title: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada’s blue wall in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: As construction for hyperscale Google AI data centres go full throttle in Visakhapatnam, farmers say promised land and jobs have not arrived

The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it.

Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage drags on as company observes ‘limited recovery’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa

Microsoft Outlook suffered a major outage across the world Thursday (November 12, 2026), with tens of thousands of users struggling to access their email as the company said it was working "aggressively" to reduce the impact.

The disruption, which Microsoft attributed to "elevated load" on its infrastructure, dragged on for much of the U.S. workday and also affected other company products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
The disruption went global within a span of an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.
A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.
Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports "in the Americas," but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected "Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."
Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.
"We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company wrote on X.
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.
"We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."
In the United States, around 130,000 users reported issues with Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time (1800 GMT), according to Downdetector.
Outage reports have since declined, with about 37,000 users reporting experiencing issues with Outlook as of 6 pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT).
Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), ending his 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China .

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. articles.title: MP alleges intelligence failure over Nanjangud drug racket
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar has accused the Congress government of a serious intelligence failure following the alleged busting of an inter-State drug racket operating under the guise of a banana plantation in Nanjangud by the Keralam Police.

In a statement here, Mr. Yaduveer said it was shocking that the racket operating on Karnataka soil was detected by the police of a neighbouring State rather than the Karnataka Police or the State intelligence wing.

He said this was not an isolated incident, pointing out that Maharashtra Police and central investigating agencies had intervened in recent years to expose organised drug networks operating in Mysuru. “Such incidents raised serious questions about the effectiveness of the State’s intelligence machinery,” he added.

Questioning the government’s repeated claims of intensifying its crackdown on narcotics and strengthening police surveillance, he asked how an illegal operation allegedly conducted under the cover of agricultural activity could go unnoticed by the local police.

He alleged that the repeated involvement of police forces from other States and central agencies in detecting alleged criminal networks operating in Karnataka reflected serious lapses in law enforcement and intelligence gathering. The Congress government should take moral responsibility for the failure, he demanded.

Mr. Yaduveer also sought to know why the State intelligence wing had failed to detect the racket, what surveillance mechanisms were in place to identify organised drug networks and who would be held accountable for the alleged lapses.

Calling for a comprehensive investigation, he urged the government to uncover the entire network behind the racket, fix accountability for the alleged intelligence lapses, strengthen inter-State police coordination and take stringent action against all those involved.

articles.title: Swachh Survekshan: Guntur wins ‘Super Swachh League’ award
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Guntur finishes third among cities with a population of three lakh to 10 lakh under the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 rankings
Guntur has won the ‘Super Swachh League’ award after finishing third among cities with a population of three lakh to 10 lakh under the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 rankings.

Guntur Municipal Corporation Commissioner K. Mayur Ashok received the award from President Droupadi Murmu at a ceremony held at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi on Wednesday, along with Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana, Principal Secretary S. Suresh Kumar and APTIDCO Managing Director B. Sunil Kumar Reddy.
Andhra Pradesh has secured six national awards, emerging as the second-best performing State in the country.

Mr. Ashok attributed the achievement to the collective efforts of municipal officials, sanitation workers and public participation. He said several initiatives had been implemented to improve sanitation and scientific waste management in the city.

A waste-to-energy plant is operational, while a Letter of Award has been issued for establishing a new Bio-CBG plant to generate green energy from waste. The civic body has also introduced electric autos, compactors and modern sweeping machines to strengthen garbage collection, he said.
Scientific removal of legacy waste, the ‘Swarnandhra-Swachh Andhra’ programme and the 30-day ‘Operation Clean Sweep’ drive contributed to improving urban cleanliness, he said.
The Municipal Commissioner pledged to continue efforts to transform Guntur into a cleaner and better-maintained city.

articles.title: Recent repairs on OMR come undone
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Sholinganallur junction has a bad stretch of road that is riddled with potholes; portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart

Portions of Rajiv Gandhi Salai and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road continue to have bad patches and potholes that make driving on these roads difficult. These are the sections where the Chennai Metro Rail works are under way.
V. Raman, a resident of Mettukuppam, said the worst spot was the Sholinganallur junction.

“I drive a van at times and many commuters like me have to slowdown at this spot. This leads to considerable slow down of traffic flow. It is worse during school hours with more vehicles on road. Service lanes are in a bad shape,” he said. The Sholinganallur junction has a particularly bad patch that is riddled with potholes. Repairs undertaken recently seem to have come undone, said Krishna Suresh, a resident of Karapakkam.

“A lot of small-sized blue metal have come loose from both the OMR and the Medavakkam-Sholinganallur Road. At times, the stones hit vehicles. Pedestrians find it very difficult to walk due to damages along the road,” he said.
Co-founder of Federation of OMR Residents Associations Harsha Koda said that portions of OMR that were re-laid in February have come apart.
“The height of the road was unnecessarily increased. No study on rainwater flow was done before the re-laying, which is why it has led to flooding. We need an independent flood-risk study.”

articles.title: Low-pressure area likely to form over Bay of Bengal, ease rain deficit in State
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Regional Meteorological Centre watches next weather system likely for rainfall prospects over Tamil Nadu

The season’s next low-pressure area is likely to form over the southeast Bay of Bengal around Friday and intensify into a depression by November 15, raising expectations of widespread rainfall to overcome shortfall in various districts and boost water sources.
The Regional Meteorological Centre has so far forecast moderate rainfall over southern districts till November 15, with rainfall likely to shift to north Tamil Nadu next week.

November is the wettest month of the year for many districts, including Chennai, Nagapattinam, Cuddalore and Tiruchi, which receive their maximum share of annual rainfall during this time. This Northeast monsoon, districts like Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai, Thanjavur, Chengalpattu and Tiruvarur, are among the districts that continue to record a rainfall deficit.

The weather agency has said an upper air cyclonic circulation over south Andaman Sea and neighbourhood is expected to trigger the formation of a low pressure area over southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday. It is further likely to gather strength as depression by November 15.
Officials of the RMC, however, noted that the rainfall impact zone could be identified only after the system gains strength and its direction becomes clearer.
V.R.Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said the weather agency is monitoring for chances of the system becoming a cyclone and the prospects of rainfall over TN.

“Normally, the weather systems that form over southwest Bay of Bengal have a tendency to move towards Tamil Nadu. Cyclone Murasu also had its genesis in the same region as the upcoming system. The initial circulation that influenced Cyclone Murasu was over south Andaman sea. We will get more clarity on its movement in one or two days,” he said.

The current weather pattern in parts of the State is being influenced by an upper air cyclonic circulation over Gulf of Mannar and neighbourhood. The RMC has retained its forecast of moderate rainfall over south and delta districts till Sunday. Those in north coastal belt may receive light rainfall till Sunday and witness an increase in rainfall intensity from November 16.
However, prospects of widespread and heavy rainfall would depend on the track and intensity of the fresh weather system, officials added.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Deadlines to the two rounds were last extended in September by about two months to November 15.

The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: VS Hospitals introduces digital mammography system for breast cancer detection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The system uses a 50-micron detector to capture detailed images of breast tissue, helping radiologists examine tiny microcalcifications that may be associated with early breast abnormalities
VS Hospitals has introduced a new 2D digital mammography system to strengthen breast cancer screening and diagnosis.

The AMULET SOPHINITY system from Fujifilm uses a high-resolution detector with a pixel size of 50 microns, allowing detailed imaging of breast tissue, including tiny microcalcifications, which can sometimes be an early indicator of breast abnormalities.

Mammography uses low-dose X-rays to examine breast tissue and can help identify abnormalities that may not be detectable through physical examination. The new system has intelligent exposure control, which adjusts X-ray exposure according to breast composition while maintaining image quality. AI-based positioning support is designed to assist in accurate positioning and consistent image acquisition.

The equipment takes approximately five seconds for standard image acquisition and 12 seconds for high-resolution imaging. It also has features such as flexible positioning, intelligent breast compression and automatic decompression to help reduce discomfort during the examination.

Speaking at the launch, S. Subramanian, Chairman and Managing Director of V.S. Hospitals, said early detection was important in breast cancer care and that mammography played a key role in identifying breast abnormalities.
The hospital will offer free mammography screening to underprivileged people throughout November 2026. Those seeking to avail themselves of the screening can contact the hospital at 7448850500.

articles.title: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng says she has been stopped from coming to Hyderabad for Bharat Summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ms. Lyng says she has been denied entry into India despite having a visa
Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng, who works for the Oslo-based daily newspaper Dagsavisen , has said that she has been stopped from coming to India despite having a valid visa.

“I got a visa to India and was supposed to leave this morning to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. I had been invited as a panellist and speaker on the future of media and press freedom. But «orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa,” she said in a post on X, on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

“I was supposed to speak on media, press freedom and democracy and how they are intertwined,” she spoke in the video message where she puts the onus on India’s Home Minister Amit Shah to let her come as 48 hours are still there for her session.

I got a visa to India and was supposed to leave this morning to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. I had been invited as a panelist and speaker on the future of media and press freedom. But «orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa. Here is my message for @AmitShah
She linked the refusal to let her into India to the freedom of press question she posed in Norway to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in May 2026.

Ms. Lyng has been listed as a speaker on Day 2 of the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on November 14 in a session that will have Leonard Novy, director, Institute for Media and Communications, Sangeeta Baruah Pisharoty, president of the Press Club of India and Francesco Lapenta director of Institute of Future and Innovation Studies. The session will be moderated by Pawan Khera, MP and chairperson of INC Communications.

The Indian Embassy in Norway has not released any statement about the denial of permission. “The embassy in Norway is not at fault. They were truly nice and helpful during the process. It is the Ministry of Home Affairs that has ruined the trip by denying me entry even though I have gotten a visa and had political clearance for the conference,” she wrote in another social media past.

articles.title: Karnataka Minister Eshwar Khandre asks officials to blacklist Larsen & Toubro for ‘delaying’ works
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has directed that Larsen & Toubro Limited be blacklisted for alleged slow progress of work in drinking water projects
Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre has directed that Larsen & Toubro Limited (L&T) be blacklisted for alleged slow progress of work in drinking water projects.

The direction came after the final notice issued to the company that is executing drinking water facilities to 388 rural habitations in Dharwad district, Kalghatgi town, and eight en route rural habitations of Saundatti taluk, Belagavi district from the Renukasagar reservoir (Navilutheertha dam).

Sources said that though the work was awarded on April 20, 2022, to be completed by October 19, 2024, the progress on site was very slow. The daily pipeline progress is also less than 500 m per day, sources said.

It is learnt that instruction had been issued to complete trial run of all 126 villages, which are not affected by the proposals submitted by the Forest Department, to be completed within December, 2026, and the company was instructed to submit detailed week-wise completion plan for pipe procurement, laying, hydro testing and trial run.

Sources said that the officials informed the Minister during a meeting that despite the instructions, pipes allegedly had not been purchased, adequate number of workers had not been deployed and work was progressing slow, and that progress report was not being submitted.

In response, the Minister asked officials to black list L& T and issue final notice to all contractors who were delaying implementation of work, especially at a time when the State was reeling under drought.

articles.title: Keralam government centralising power in Chief Minister’s office: Pinarayi Vijayan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has accused the Keralam government of concentrating decision-making powers in the hands of the Chief Minister, alleging that even ministers are being kept in the dark about important decisions.
He said the situation was unprecedented in the State and called for a judicial investigation into what he described as suspicious administrative actions.

Speaking at the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] political explanation meeting at Chathurakkinar in Madikkai, Mr. Vijayan questioned how a Minister, who is also the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee president, could remain unaware of major decisions concerning his own department. He said governance was being conducted without proper coordination between departments, with the Chief Minister taking decisions independently.

Referring to the electricity purchase agreement with GNA, Mr. Vijayan said the Minister concerned had earlier said that he was unaware of the decision to enter into the agreement. The Minister was reportedly unaware even when the decision to abandon the agreement was taken, he said.
He also alleged that attempts were being made to create an artificial power shortage to benefit corporate monopolies.

articles.title: Kerala High Court orders government to ready adequate medicines, vehicles at mental health centres by November 24
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Stating that assurances alone are not sufficient, and they have to translate into action, the Kerala High Court has directed the government to make available adequate medicines and vehicles in mental health centres by November 24.

A Division Bench of Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji, who had earlier this year visited the centres in Thiruvananthapuram, Thrissur, and Kozhikode acceded to the Advocate General’s request to file an action taken report by the same day on the construction of compound walls and the appointment of necessary personnel at the centres.

This was after the Advocate General submitted that the construction of compound walls around the centres was progressing at a good speed. On the appointment of personnel, he sought another two weeks’ time, saying that there had been a change of incumbent in the post of Secretary, Health and Family Welfare department, and that he was in the process of evaluating the files concerned. The matter has been listed for hearing on November 24.

The High Court had in September expressed satisfaction at the government’s decision to rename mental health centres as “happiness and wellness centres”, observing that the (hitherto) stigmatisation of patients, their caregivers, and the centres as a whole was something one could not be oblivious to. The Advocate General had informed the court then that the government was looking into infrastructure and staff vacancy issues at the centres with ‘full sincerity’.

articles.title: Great Trigonometrical Survey stations in Tamil Nadu documented, published in five volumes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Department of Survey and Settlement and the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology have documented the Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) stations in the State and published the documentation in five volumes.

According to an official release, during British rule, the Great Trigonometrical Survey was launched by Colonel William Lambton at St. Thomas Mount in Chennai on April 10, 1802. The survey continued for 70 years until 1871 using theodolite instruments. As part of the exercise, Great Trigonometrical Survey stations were established across India, including at several locations in Tamil Nadu. These stations are under the jurisdiction of the Survey of India.

The Tamil Nadu government granted permission for a comprehensive exercise to identify all the GTS stations in the State, conduct surveys, map and document them, and take steps to preserve them. The initiative also aims to facilitate future modern surveying activities in the State by using the geo-coordinates of these stations.
Accordingly, officials from the Department of Survey and Settlement and TNSDA jointly conducted an extensive field survey, identified all the GTS stations in Tamil Nadu and documented their details.

Based on their documentation, they have published five volumes titled ‘Documentation of the Great Trigonometrical Survey Stations in Tamil Nadu’. With the objective of ensuring the preservation of the GTS stations in the districts, the Director of Survey and Settlement has distributed the volumes to District Collectors and district-level officials of the Survey Department, the release added.

articles.title: Daughter of Cheranalloor accident victim files review petition before Kerala High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bhadrakeerthi R.J., daughter of Jayabalakrishnan who died after a luxury car reportedly driven by the minor son of a judicial officer rammed his two-wheeler at Cheranalloor here on October 25, has filed a criminal review petition before the Kerala High Court, challenging an order passed on November 5 by the Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Judge (Children’s Court) granting bail to the minor in conflict with law (CCL).

In her petition, she submitted that the impugned judgment of the children’s court is ex facie illegal, perverse, and vitiated by a complete non-application of mind to the mandatory statutory exceptions embedded in the proviso to S.12(1) of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.

The court erred in holding that the gravity of the offence and the loss of human life cannot be factored into the assessment under the Section, whose proviso explicitly mandates the denial of bail, if release is likely to ‘defeat the ends of justice’ or ‘expose the child to moral, physical or psychological danger’. In high-fatality culpable homicide cases under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita committed through gross vehicular recklessness, releasing the CCL severely undermines public confidence in the rule of law and directly defeats the ends of justice, she said in her plea.

National & Polity Report: Daughter of Cheranalloor accident victim files review petition before Kerala High Court. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and administrative governance framework.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary procedures, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and constitutional bodies responsible for upholding statutory mandates.

fullParagraphs: Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) and the Kochi-based SFO Technologies Private Limited have unveiled what is claimed to be the country’s first indigenously designed and manufactured hybrid laser arc welding (HLAW) technology.
