articles.title: Collector calls for coordinated efforts among departments to make Kurnool drug-free
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing a meeting, A. Siri directs officials to take strict action against those involved in the illegal trade

The Kurnool district administration has intensified its fight against drug trafficking and consumption, with Collector A. Siri directing officials to take strict action against those involved in the illegal trade.

At a Narcotics Coordination Centre meeting held at the Collectorate on Wednesday, the Collector and Superintendent of Police (SP) Vikrant Patil called for coordinated efforts by the police, education, excise, medical and welfare departments to make the district drug-free.

The Collector urged Education Department officials to conduct awareness programmes in all government and private schools, junior colleges and higher educational institutions. Students identified as drug users should be given confidential counselling and rehabilitation support. Officials were also told to identify school dropouts and prevent them from falling into drug abuse.

Meanwhile, the administration has identified 30 dark spots in Kurnool city for the installation of streetlights and CCTV cameras. Joharapuram Road, Fish Area and Bangarupeta have been identified as sensitive locations requiring special surveillance.

The SP said that police had conducted nine cordon and search operations and surprise checks under Operation Trishul. Three drug-related cases were registered this month. Police seized 1.5 kg of ganja in Taluka limits, 20 grams of MDMA in Veldurthi, and another 1.5 kg of ganja during an excise operation.

articles.title: Banana festival to showcase rare varieties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: To promote the diversity of indigenous bananas, their cultivation and associated food culture, Sahaja Samrudha, in collaboration with the Department of Horticulture, Karnataka State Agricultural Produce Processing and Export Corporation Limited (KAPPEC), ICAR–JSS Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Suttur, and Abhay Naturals, is organising a Banana Festival on November 14 and 15 at Nanjaraja Bahadur Choultry in Mysuru.

The two-day Banana Festival will be inaugurated by Venkataramana Reddy J. Patil, managing director, Karnataka State Agricultural Produce Processing and Export Corporation Limited (KAPPEC). Giridhar Parvatam, director of CSIR–Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI), Mysuru, will launch the Banana Bharat mobile application.

More than 150 banana varieties will be showcased at the festival. Visitors can purchase fresh bananas of several traditional varieties, including Nanjangud Rasabale, Nendran, Elakki Bale, Finger Banana, Kamalapur Red Banana, Karpuravalli, Poovan, Chandra Bale, Madarangi and Red Banana. Quality banana planting materials will also be available for those interested in cultivating bananas.

Daya Prasad from Sullia, who has conserved around 400 banana varieties, will bring some rare varieties from his collection for public display. Ram Prasad Hegde from Sirsi, a national award-winning plant conservationist, will also showcase rare banana varieties and planting materials. An eight-foot-long Sahasra Bale and a red banana variety whose entire plant appears as though it has been set on fire will be among the major attractions of the festival, according to press release.

A training programme on banana cultivation and opportunities for value addition will be held at 2:00 p.m on Saturday. At 10:30 am on Sunday, a children’s drawing competition and a banana-based cooking competition will be organised. Interested participants can take part. For more information, contact Ashok – 9632770473.

articles.title: Collectors to closely monitor comprehensive land resurvey: Ponguleti
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy directed district Collectors to closely monitor the comprehensive land resurvey and take an active role in resolving land-related issues at the field level.

At a video conference with Collectors, Additional Collectors, Revenue Divisional Officers and Survey Department officials on Wednesday, the Minister asked Collectors to visit villages regularly, interact with farmers and explain the survey process and the mechanism available for raising objections after the completion of the survey.

He directed officials to conduct public announcements in villages once every 15 days after issuing notices, so that landowners were aware of the opportunity to register their objections. Officials should also immediately communicate the extent of land recorded in revenue records and the extent established through the resurvey to the respective landowners, he said.
Mr. Srinivasa Reddy said Palair constituency had been selected as a pilot project, with the resurvey being taken up in all 141 revenue villages under its jurisdiction.

The Minister said the government had already issued a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the exercise, but variations in its implementation had been reported from different areas. Based on feedback, the SOP would be suitably modified.

He said a recent meeting with field officials from Siddipet, Medak and Sangareddy districts had focused on discrepancies in land extent, government lands and other disputes in villages where the survey had been completed or notices issued.

While appreciating the performance of the Collectors of Nalgonda and Khammam districts in conducting the resurvey, he expressed dissatisfaction with the progress in Nizamabad and asked the officials concerned to improve their performance and expedite the exercise in line with the targets.

Expressing concern over the continued pendency of issues relating to lands listed under Section 22-A, he said the government had already issued clear instructions on resolving them. Collectors should take special initiative to examine individual cases at the field level. Revenue Secretary D.S. Lokesh Kumar and Housing Secretary V.P. Gautam were present.

articles.title: Netanyahu dismisses claims that Israel blocking supplies to Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Benjamin Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Donald Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected accusations that Israel has been delaying the entry of winter supplies into the Gaza Strip as the enclave faces worsening conditions this week, with severe rains flooding makeshift tents.
He said Israel was not to blame for the worsening conditions for Palestinians in Gaza's tent camps that have been hit by severe winter floods.

His remarks came after the U.S.-created Board of Peace — established under U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Israel-Hamas war and oversee Gaza's recovery — said Monday (November 9, 2026) that Israel's delaying of the entry of winter supplies into Gaza had “exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge”.

Torrential rain has battered the war-torn enclave in recent days, damaging tens of thousands of makeshift tents. Four people, including three children, were killed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) when a large sandstone slab collapsed onto tents during the rains.

Mr. Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Mr. Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes.
“Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza, and it is now cynically exploiting that suffering to shift blame onto Israel once again,” he said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the situation in Gaza was “intolerable” and demanded Israel end “arbitrary restrictions” on aid. And in Washington, Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii, the top Democrat on the Senate's foreign spending subcommittee, called for Israel to immediately allow winter gear into Gaza.

“There are a lot of challenges when it comes to Israel and Palestine that are complicated, and fraught, and contentious,” Mr. Schatz said on the Senate floor on Tuesday (November 10, 2026). “But we should all be able to agree that repairing torn tents and helping people to dry out, and providing warmth to freezing children is a basic human obligation.”

articles.title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta, sees no deliberate election bias
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Meta told the Court last month it had adopted ​measures to ensure equal treatment of ‌the two campaigns

Brazil's electoral authority fined Meta's Facebook 7.5 million reais ($1.34 million) for failing to fully comply ​with judicial orders during last month's Presidential election runoff campaign, but said there ‌was no evidence so far that the company had ​deliberately acted to influence the outcome.

In a unanimous decision, ⁠the country's top electoral court (TSE) ruled on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that Facebook had failed to adequately meet court demands related to allegations that its ‌platform treated content from the rival campaigns of leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator ‌Flavio Bolsonaro differently.

Mr. Lula's coalition filed a complaint ahead of the ‌vote alleging ⁠restrictions on the distribution of its posts, the activity ⁠of purportedly inauthentic accounts, failures in identifying AI-generated content, and asymmetries in the operation of Meta's tools.
Meta told the Court last month it had adopted ​measures to ensure equal treatment of ‌the two campaigns. It did not immediately reply to a fresh request for comment.

The Court said Meta had provided some information and documents on the measures, but found that ‌parts of its orders were either not complied with, were ​only partially fulfilled, or were carried out after deadlines had passed.

"The records contain technical failures acknowledged ⁠by Facebook itself, but there are no elements allowing us to conclude, on a preliminary basis, that there was deliberate action to unbalance ‌the election," Justice Marco Aurelio Bellizze wrote in his ruling.
"That conclusion would require robust evidence, to be produced through the appropriate legal proceedings," he added.

According to Mr. Bellizze, the fine reflected Meta's conduct in responding to the Court orders as a whole, including delays, incomplete information and difficulties in verifying some of ‌the data submitted.

The amount corresponds to three daily fines of 500,000 reais between October ​17 and 19, and six days of fines of 1 million reais per day between October 20 ⁠and 25, when Mr. Lula unexpectedly secured re-election over Mr. Bolsonaro after his ⁠team mobilised a huge social media campaign.

Mr. Lula has long vowed to tighten rules on social media in the country. ‌In his victory speech, he said, "We had to overcome foreign interference in the election, coming from outside through digital platforms ​that we will have to regulate."

articles.title: Central committee suggests three-year roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand mining from active river channels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems

The Supreme Court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) has suggested preparing a time-bound roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years.

The committee, a statutory body since 2023 and originally formed in 2002 on the apex court's order, has also recommended developing sustainable alternative sources of sand and aggregates to progressively reduce dependence on extraction from active river channels.
For this, it has suggested scientific desiltation of dams and reservoirs and recycling of construction and demolition (C&D) waste, among other measures.
These recommendations are part of the CEC's report submitted to the Supreme Court on November 2 as part of a sou motu case related to illegal sand mining in the National Chambal Sanctuary.

In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems.

"The impacts inter alia include riverbed degradation and infrastructure vulnerability, depletion of groundwater and loss of aquifers, destruction of aquatic and riparian habitats, and alteration of river morphology and hydrology, etc," said the committee.
It also highlights that there is no consolidated, reliable national database that quantifies the volume or value of illegally extracted river sand.
As a result, the CEC has recommended strengthening the existing regulatory and monitoring framework governing extraction from permissible areas.

This can be done through scientific identification of mineable stretches, regular replenishment studies, determination of sustainable extraction limits, environmental safeguards, digital tracking of mineral transportation and end-use and effective enforcement, it said.

"A time-bound roadmap shall be prepared to progressively phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years, alongside development of adequate alternative sources, including reservoir sediment, M-sand and recycled C&D waste, while ensuring that legitimate construction requirements are met,” the CEC said in its report.

Moreover, the committee has said that there is an urgent need to develop sustainable alternative sources of sand and aggregates to progressively reduce dependence on extraction from active river channels.

"State governments shall promote the production and use of manufactured sand (M-Sand) through suitable incentives and quality certification, establish facilities for processing and recycling construction and demolition (C&D) waste into sand and aggregates, and permit recovery of sand and other materials from floodplains," suggested the CEC.

articles.title: Prix Pascal: If AI writes your book, are you still a writer?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: France’s new Prix Pascal for AI-assisted books prompts a writer to reflect on the slow pleasures of making art, loss of individuality, and need to reclaim human imagination

There is now a new French literary prize for AI-assisted writing — the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA. The Pascal prize requires entrants to turn in an unpublished manuscript, fiction or non-fiction, in French, of approximately 3,00,000 characters, written with the help of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Writers must declare which AI model and prompts they have employed. The applications, to be submitted by November 30, consist of “a seed, a manuscript and a technical file, submitted simultaneously”. Ten finalists will be announced on December 4 and the winner will be revealed on December 15.

“This [submitted] work must be useful, or raise awareness, or help to solve in an original way one of the ecological, social and ethical challenges that threaten humanity. AI can now solve previously unsolvable mathematical problems. Here, it is asked to produce a text that will help humanity progress towards wisdom and the preservation of itself and its environment.”

I love the way in which the manifesto strategically reframes tacit support for what goes against the very grain of the creative spirit as an essentially moral and ethical act. But of course! This is the way these things are usually done. The prize was founded by Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant and Gilles Mentré. The first two are technology entrepreneurs, which too is no surprise.

Notwithstanding their precarity, writers and artists have always been viewed with a combination of envy, fear and hatred. The imagination is a dangerous thing. It is ungovernable. It cannot easily be controlled or colonised. It does not seek permission. And that, to many, is frightening. What better way to colonise the imagination than to introduce AI into the writer’s world? Also, that way everybody — even the ones with little understanding of what a writer does — can acquire the overnight label of one. Where does this leave writers who have spent years honing their craft, writers who have survived by the skin of their teeth? The world needs writers more urgently than ever before, and more of us should let some form of creative practice into our lives.

Two semesters ago, a few students from my Creative Writing course, at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai, confessed to what their worst fears were: that, having come of age in the post-AI era, they would find it a challenge to access and exercise their imagination — which, in their understanding, was foundational to the course. I was struck by their capacity for self-reflection, moved by what they recognised, quite rightly, as an imminent loss. This, too, is the other dark side of what we have got ourselves into: the loss of imagination is foundational not just to the stray creative writing course but to life itself.

The argument that it is best not to be left behind, that AI is here to stay so writers must take the good things it has to offer and navigate the rest, is a specious one. The folks making this argument may be right about the inevitability of AI, but does that make any of it less disturbing or a tad more ethical? I don’t see how one can frame this as anything other than a pure black-and-white story. If you give AI an inch, it is very likely that you will take a mile from yourself.

It is a slippery slope. You start by using AI as an instrument — perhaps to help you rewrite a sentence — and before you know it, you are likely to seek its help extensively to write the entire piece. Who then is the real author of the piece? After all, it is in the writing that writers do their thinking. I don’t think the answer lies in declaring AI use upfront. While this may address the ethical question to a small extent, it still does not change the fact that we are always going to ‘writing’ with training wheels on. The craft is in the writing and if you give that away what is left?

There is another problem too: that of the asymmetry between the writer on whose work an LLM is trained and the user who then draws on that work to write in “collaboration with” that particular AI model. The original writer whose consent has very likely not been sought gets nothing from this entire process — a process which de-humanises creative work and repurposes it as training data.

Artificial intelligence illustrations are seen on a lapto with books in the background in this illustration photo on 18 July, 2023. (Photo by Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | Photo Credit: Getty Images

As almost everyone from editors of literary journals on the brink of closure to writing teachers will tell you, it is often impossible to tell AI-assisted writing apart from human writing. In fact, you may find that some AI-assisted writing may be as good as if not better than writing by humans. It, of course, depends on the prompts used and how advanced the models are.

The LLMs have been trained to mimic human syntax, and because humans frequently edit AI text or may even adopt AI-like phrasing, it is impossible to be absolutely certain which is which. Neither dedicated AI-detection tools nor human readers are able to establish clearly whether a piece of writing is AI-generated or authored by a human. Worse still, detection tools often throw up false positives. This is especially true when it comes to non-native English writing. There are also ways to bypass detectors. OpenAI, however, discontinued its own native AI detection tool in 2023 because of low accuracy rates.

We are often told that AI-assisted text tends to exhibit certain stylistic patterns such as the em dash — which, incidentally, I use a lot — that you will find in it the overuse of certain words such as “delve” and parallel contrast structures such as “It is not just X, it is Y” or that it lacks “soul”. All these arguments were used in the controversy over Jamir Nazir’s 2026 Granta-Commonwealth Short Story Prize-winning entry “The Serpent in the Grove”.

articles.title: New registration framework proposed to strengthen allied and healthcare professions in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions invites public and stakeholder comments on the Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Union Ministry of Health, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the registration of allied and healthcare professionals, with pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment, and transition to regular registration.

The broad categories of allied and healthcare professions governed by the NCAHP include clinical laboratories, surgical and emergency technology, physiotherapy, nutrition, ophthalmology, occupational therapy, community and behavioural health, medical imaging, physician associates, and health informatics.

The proposed framework aims for uniformity, transparency and accountability in professional registration. Practitioners can enhance their competencies in keeping with prescribed standards, a release issued by the Ministry said.
Key features of the proposed regulations include the establishment of a standardised mechanism for provisional registration in accordance with the NCAHP Act, 2021.

“Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable, to meet the requirements for regular registration,’’ the Healthy Ministry’s statement said.

articles.title: German military to stop using Chinese-made drones, citing security concerns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Drones from Chinese manufacturers had previously been permitted as a cost-effective option for target practice and training purposes; they will now be replaced with European products

Germany's military will no longer use Chinese-made drones, ​a defence ministry spokesperson said on Wednesday, amid mounting concern ‌among Western militaries that they could pose a ​security risk and be used to transmit ⁠sensitive information to Beijing.

Drones from Chinese manufacturers had previously been permitted as a cost-effective option for target practice and training purposes, ‌the spokesperson said. They will now be replaced with European products.
"To strengthen the Bundeswehr's ‌self-sufficiency and technological sovereignty, Chinese-made models will no ‌longer ⁠be used," the spokesperson said in an emailed ⁠statement.

There is no blanket ban on the use of systems from specific countries, the spokesperson said, adding the decision is based on ​individual risk assessments ‌aimed at safeguarding military security, IT and data security.
China's foreign ministry told Reuters that it opposed Germany's "discriminatory practice" targeting Chinese products.
Germany's Der Spiegel news outlet first ‌reported the change.

Local commanders had been allowed ​to purchase the drones under a 2024 strategy that included a "white list" of approved systems, ⁠including several made by China-based DJI, the world's largest drone maker, Spiegel reported.

DJI has repeatedly said its ‌drones do not pose a security risk and in May the company told US lawmakers that an independent review had found "no evidence of data transmission outside the United States".

The US last month prohibited vehicles made by China's BYD on its air base on Japan's ‌Okinawa island, and Poland in February banned Chinese-made vehicles from ​military facilities over concerns their sensors could be used to collect sensitive data.

The spokesperson said the ⁠German defence ministry had no general ban on vehicles from ⁠specific countries or manufacturers, but said sensors installed in modern vehicles are seen as potential security ‌risks, and therefore access to sensitive military sites can be restricted where necessary.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier

The Democratic Republic of Congo's worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), as armed conflict hampers the response.
The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier.
It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health.
Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever.
Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years.
The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020.
The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu.
Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.
No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak.

Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo.
Security in eastern DRC is another challenge in fighting the health crisis.
Ituri province is one of the most volatile and clashes between armed groups and violence against health workers regularly occur.

articles.title: Italy evacuates over 300 schools due to bomb alert, with threats in Scotland and Ireland
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni said there was no indication of any “concrete danger” to schools and that the threats appeared aimed at “generating alarm and concern”

Italian authorities evacuated hundreds of schools on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) after an emailed bomb threat, the latest in a series of disruptions affecting European institutions following recent hoaxes aimed at airlines and broadcasters.
Schools in Ireland, Scotland and Northern Ireland received similar threats, but no evacuations were reported.

Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni said there was no indication of any “concrete danger” to schools and that the threats appeared aimed at “generating alarm and concern”. She said investigations were underway and that she had called a meeting of ministers for later Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

The anonymous email also threatened Ms. Meloni, according to copies obtained by Italian media, including the LaPresse news agency. She did not address the personal threat in her statement, and her office had no immediate comment.

The email purported to come from the leader of an otherwise unknown group with an anti-woman name and contained particularly violent threats. It was signed with the same Russian name used in last week's threats against European broadcasters.
Authorities have not attributed the threats to any group or state, and no evidence has emerged linking the hoaxes to a government.

Police in Northern Ireland said they were conducting “urgent inquiries” after a threatening email was sent to hundreds of schools. Police in Scotland said they were treating similar messages as hoaxes and were not requiring schools to evacuate.
“Our assessment remains that they do not represent a credible threat,” Police Scotland said.
Police in Ireland also said they were aware of a “generic communication” sent to several educational institutions.
Italian Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara told reporters that 312 schools had been evacuated after receiving email threats.

“These are very delicate considerations, because there is always the risk that there is someone else behind the madman,” he said. “Given that so many schools are involved, the real risk is almost non-existent.”
At Rome's Mamiani high school, students poured into the streets, mistaking the alarm for the recess bell. They learned of the bomb threat only after they were outside.

articles.title: COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels

Wars and trade disputes should not be allowed to distract the world from ​its struggle to combat global warming, the leaders of Brazil and Turkey told the COP31 climate conference ⁠on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

"A year ago, the planet left COP30 invigorated... (but) this momentum has dropped off at the start of this year. Climate change disappeared from the speeches and documents from global leadership," Brazil's President Luiz ‌Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year's conference, told the summit.
"We started talking more about weapons ‌and ⁠tariffs than the survival of future generations," he said. "The planet cannot be in the mercy of ⁠hegemonic struggles."
"Wars, crises, migration, famine and poverty increase the need for international solidarity each day," he said.
The U.S. and Israeli war on Iran this year has disrupted West Asia crude oil shipments and sent fuel prices soaring around the ​globe, triggering a scramble for reliable supplies.

Those dynamics ‌have pushed global warming down the list of urgent priorities for some governments, even as climate advocates argue they make the perfect case for a more rapid adoption of clean energy alternatives to oil.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told ​world leaders earlier in the day that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction, and that fast action was needed to ⁠avert it.

"The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. This is the path to mutually assured destruction," Mr. Guterres said, pointing to rising emissions, global temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters.

A UN report last month found ‌the world on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

Meanwhile, 2026 has also stood out with a series of extreme heatwaves across Western Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a catastrophic flood killing more than 1,450 people, with thousands still missing.

Former French Prime Minister Laurent Fabius, who presided over the 2015 Paris climate conference and leads an advisory council of former COP presidents, said the leaders' speeches should give political impetus to the ‌negotiations.

COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels

Wars and trade disputes should not be allowed to distract the world from ​its struggle to combat global warming, the leaders of Brazil and Turkey told the COP31 climate conference ⁠on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

"A year ago, the planet left COP30 invigorated... (but) this momentum has dropped off at the start of this year. Climate change disappeared from the speeches and documents from global leadership," Brazil's President Luiz ‌Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year's conference, told the summit.

"We started talking more about weapons ‌and ⁠tariffs than the survival of future generations," he said. "The planet cannot be in the mercy of ⁠hegemonic struggles."

"Wars, crises, migration, famine and poverty increase the need for international solidarity each day," he said.

The U.S. and Israeli war on Iran this year has disrupted West Asia crude oil shipments and sent fuel prices soaring around the ​globe, triggering a scramble for reliable supplies.

Those dynamics ‌have pushed global warming down the list of urgent priorities for some governments, even as climate advocates argue they make the perfect case for a more rapid adoption of clean energy alternatives to oil.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told ​world leaders earlier in the day that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction, and that fast action was needed to ⁠avert it.

"The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. This is the path to mutually assured destruction," Mr. Guterres said, pointing to rising emissions, global temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters.

A UN report last month found ‌the world on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

Meanwhile, 2026 has also stood out with a series of extreme heatwaves across Western Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a catastrophic flood killing more than 1,450 people, with thousands still missing.

Former French Prime Minister Laurent Fabius, who presided over the 2015 Paris climate conference and leads an advisory council of former COP presidents, said the leaders' speeches should give political impetus to the ‌negotiations.

articles.title: ‘Iran will not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington

Iran will not allow even a single ​particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country, and there ‌will be consequences in the event of any ​new U.S. strikes on the Islamic Republic, Iranian ⁠security chief Mohsen Rezaei said in televised remarks.

Mr. Rezaei was speaking to Lebanon's pro-Iranian Al Mayadeen TV after U.S. officials downplayed the need ‌for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the ‌Republicans' defeat in the November 3 midterm elections.
Mr. Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington.
"Any new U.S. attacks will also be met with targeting U.S. bases far away," he said.
Iran's Supreme Leader has issued a directive ​that the country's near-weapons-grade uranium ‌should not be sent abroad, two senior Iranian sources said in May.

"We need the enriched material to design ships and submarines that work on nuclear energy", Mr. Rezaei said, ‌adding that Tehran has informed Moscow that its enriched ​nuclear material will remain in the country and "we will use it ourselves".
Russia has previously offered to ⁠remove uranium from Iran as part of a potential deal to ease U.S. concerns, but said it was for Tehran to ‌decide whether to remove it or not.

The IAEA estimates that Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60% — a level far higher than needed for civilian use — when Israel and the U.S. attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. How much of that has survived is ‌unclear.
Israel, the United States and other Western countries have long accused Iran ​of seeking nuclear weapons. Iran denies the accusation.
Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of ⁠any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the war between the ⁠two countries.
Iran has sent the United States a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only ‌after Washington meets seven demands which Tehran has presented, a senior Iranian official told Reuters last week.

articles.title: Navi Mumbai recognised as India’s cleanest city in latest Swachh Survekshan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Indore, ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the winners this year
Navi Mumbai has been adjudged the cleanest city in India at a central government awards programme, while Gujarat’s Surat was second and Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh finished third.
Among cities with a population between three lakh and 10 lakh, Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain emerged as the cleanest urban centre, followed by the UT of Chandigarh and Guntur in Andhra Pradesh.
Indore, which had been ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the toppers this year.
The awards were presented by President Droupadi Murmu at an event held here.
Rewa, another city in Madhya Pradesh, emerged as the cleanest riverfront town, followed by Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) and Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh) in second and third place, respectively.
In the 10 lakh-plus population category, Greater Visakhapatnam emerged as the cleanest city, followed by Jabalpur and Lucknow.
According to the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, in the Swachh Coastal Town category, Puri in Odisha was ranked first, followed by Kerala’s Alappuzha and Maharashtra’s Ratnagiri.
Rudrapur, in Uttarakhand, emerged as the cleanest Himalayan city, while Jammu secured the second position.
Last year, Indore had topped the league, followed by Surat and Navi Mumbai. Jaipur was recognised as the cleanest city in Rajasthan, while Gwalior received the distinction in Madhya Pradesh.

Swachh Survekshan is Swacch Bharat Mission-Urban’s flagship cleanliness assessment, with the goal of improving urban sanitation, hygiene, and waste management. Over 4,751 cities participated in the latest edition.

Swachh Survekshan made several key enhancements for the 2025-26 awards, including greater emphasis on citizen feedback, expanded coverage of Urban River Fronts, Coastlines and Water bodies and focused indicators on prevention of open defecation and open urination, cleanliness of tourist and heritage hotspots, and behaviour change initiatives in schools.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: award-winning books / books and publishing / Artificial Intelligence

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Reservation / court / Caste / labour / government / Census 2027

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamil Nadu / government / politics / language / Delimitation / education / Governor / taxes and duties / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / Bharatiya Janata Party
